sections.text: Introduction

The first approval of the document no 
TB-SS-003-r0 was at 22 June1998, MPIS 
General Directorate looked at the document and revised at 06 Feb 02 for the title block content and EEHC instead of EEA to be as MPIS rules.

Preventive
maintenance is a cycle of planned inspections, tests, overhauls and servicing
activities designed to keep the Network equipment in good operating condition
and avoid breakdowns. Our goal is to achieve satisfactory service from our
electrical equipment, as economically as possible. We intend to accomplish this
through the development and implementation of a series of procedures and
inspections.

The
following designation and definitions are used in Ontario Hydro to provide a
coding system for maintenance activities. The coding system will be very
important when EEHC and it's 13 companies moves to apply a computerized maintenance work management
system.
Information

The
procedures fall into four different categories. These are defined and described
in the list of definitions in the following section. The
procedures are given the following designations:
 - Equipment
 inspections (I1, I2, I3)
 - Minor Maintenance (P1, P2, P3)
 - Major Maintenance (P4)
 - Capital Maintenance (C1)
 - Equipment Modification Procedures
 (MOD)

The intention is to
have up to P-4 Technical procedure written for each major class of equipment.
Although not always specifically stated in the Station Inspections and
Maintenance Procedures, the requirement to make necessary repairs or at least to
report deficiencies is always implied and expected.

While it is
recognized that maintenance frequencies must be adjusted, at times, to
coordinate equipment outages, efforts should be made to avoid exceeding the
recommended time between overhauls.

Following are
definitions of the various maintenance activities and inspections performed on
Network Equipment:
Equipment Inspections (I1, I2, I3)

The Inspections
detailed in MPIS documents comprise checks and tests on station equipment. They
may require readings to be taken or equipment condition reports to be made.
Usually the work can be completed without an outage. The designations " I1,
I2 and I3" are used to identify Inspections of increasing complexity on any
one piece of equipment. Where only one Inspection is required the designation II
is always used.

An I2 Inspection
incorporates the steps from the I1, along with additional checks or tests.
Similarly the I3 Inspection includes the II and I2 checks plus additional items.
The monthly station inspection should include all the items designated (M1),
while the quarterly station inspection will include the (M1) items plus those
designated (M3). There are also a few inspections designated as daily (D1) and
weekly (W1).
Minor Maintenance Procedures (P1, P2, P3)

The Minor Maintenance
Procedures detailed comprise visual checks, tests and equipment maintenance and
servicing work of a relatively minor nature. Usually an outage is required to
complete the work. The designations "P1, P2 and P3" are used to
identify the different Minor Maintenance Procedures required on any one piece of
equipment.

The " 1, 2 or 3
" do not represent time intervals but rather increasing degrees of
complexity. As with the Inspections, the P2 incorporates the P1 and the P3
incorporates the P1 and P2.
Major Maintenance Procedures (P4)

The Major Maintenance Procedures "P4", outline the
steps required for dismantling and overhauling station equipment. An outage is
always required to complete the work.
Capital Maintenance Procedures (C1)

This class of a
Routine Maintenance Procedure is used to extend the life span of aging
equipment. Usually the "C1" Equipment Rebuild Procedure comprises a
P-4 overhaul plus extra work to replace worn out components such as the bearings
in Oil Circuit Breakers (OCB'S), the "O" rings in Air Blast Breakers (ABB'S),
the contacts in Under Load tapchangers (ULTC'S), etc. Like the P4 overhauls. The
content of the "C1's" is defined by the head office functional
(operations) department in consultation with Zone staff.

The extra C1 work
should be done along with the P4, during the same outage. Of course the timing
of this work must be adjusted by the severity of the service duty, and actual
condition of the equipment.
Equipment Modification Procedures (MOD's)

"MOD's" are procedures, which outline special
modification work required to overcome some known weakness in the equipment. A
Zone in conjunction with Head Office Functional Department or committee usually
initiates them. This nonstandard work is detailed in various Technical
Directives and or Bulletins each of which require a modification to a specific
type of equipment.
Scheduling Maintenance Activities

The above definitions
describe the degree of inspection/maintenance to be performed on Network
equipment. However to establish a consistent process for maintaining equipment
it will be necessary to properly schedule these events.

Inspection and
Maintenance Schedules will be developed to show the frequency requirements for
each listed inspection and maintenance procedure. These will represent the
current "standards of maintenance" which is required on the electrical
power system. These frequencies are cross-referenced in the introduction and/or
title of each procedure, e.g. (P1-Y1), (P4-Y6), etc.

The Inspection and
Maintenance Schedule will be issued in a separate directive at a later date.

While it is
recognized that this standard may not always be met to the letter, any temporary
reduction in maintenance must be corrected as soon as possible. Should it become
necessary for anything more than a minor, short term deferral of routine
maintenance, the responsible Head Office Functional Department should be
consulted and a plan worked out to resolve the problem.
